'''Helen Lucile Nibouar''' (''[[née]]'' '''Breese'''; June 6, 1921 – December 28, 2017) was an American [[Cryptography|cryptographer]] who was part of the select group who first worked on the [[SIGABA]] cipher device during World War II. She was honored by the [[National Security Agency]]'s [[National Cryptologic Museum]] in 2012 for her role in "60 Years of Cryptologic Excellence".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://billiongraves.com/grave/Helen-B-Nibouar/8718063?referrer=myheritage|title=Billion Graves|last=Nibouar|first=Helen|access-date=29 December 2017}}</ref>

==Early life==
Nibouar grew up in Oklahoma, where she attended high school but "was unable to attend any further education." She lived with relatives for a few years before moving to Washington DC. She was inspired to volunteer her services to the US military following the bombing of [[Attack on Pearl Harbor|Pearl Harbor]].<ref name=":0" />

==Cryptography==
Nibouar had not planned to become a cryptographer, but was recruited at the water fountain by a woman who encouraged her to "give cryptography a try."<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://archive.defense.gov/news/newsarticle.aspx?id=118477|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150922101656/http://archive.defense.gov/news/newsarticle.aspx?id=118477|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 22, 2015|title=Defense.gov News Article: Cryptologists Reunite at NSA's 60th Anniversary|website=United States Department of Defense|access-date=2016-12-08}}</ref> Nibouar then trained at Morrison Field, where she met fellow cryptographer Marion Johnson.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://cryptologicfoundation.org/visit/museum/museum_exhibits/recentexhibits/60_years_excellence.html|title=NSA's 60 Years of Cryptologic Excellence Exhibit at the NCM|website=cryptologicfoundation.org|access-date=2016-12-08}}</ref> The two worked on the [[SIGABA]] cipher device, which was used to obscure troop movements and other sensitive material. They were part of a group of about five people who worked decoding these messages in Florida.<ref name=":0">{{cite conference  | first = David P. | last = Cooley | title = Interview with Helen Nibouar | publisher = National Security Agency | date = 10 August 2012 | url = https://www.nsa.gov/news-features/declassified-documents/oral-history-interviews/assets/files/nsa-oh-2012-39-nibouar.pdf | access-date = 8 December 2016 }}</ref> She later worked in Hawaii, Washington DC, Japan, and [[The Pentagon]]. She met her husband, Lieutenant Colonel Grover Cleveland Nibouar Junior, in Japan whilst assigned to the staff of General [[Douglas MacArthur]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.legacy.com/obituaries/statesman/obituary.aspx?n=grover-cleveland-nibouar&pid=167993286&fhid=4296|title=Lt. Colonel Grover Cleveland Nibouar Jr.'s Obituary on Austin American-Statesman|website=Austin American-Statesman|access-date=2016-12-08}}</ref> She then worked as the instructor, teaching cryptography to military personnel. She was particularly unusual in being able to keep her job after her marriage.<ref name=":0" />

==Later life==
Nibouar later worked as a teacher and spent a large amount of time volunteering.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://comingofageaustin.org/helen-nibouar-honored-in-washington-d-c/|title=Helen Nibouar honored in Washington D.C.|website=comingofageaustin.org|access-date=2016-12-08}}</ref> She and Marion Johnson were recognised at the ribbon-cutting ceremony for the National Cryptologic Museum exhibit on "60 Years of Cryptologic Excellence" in recognition of their work.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://hosted.verticalresponse.com/785861/dfbca612a2/TEST/TEST/|title=Pearl Harbor Program, NSA's 60th Anniversary, & More|website=hosted.verticalresponse.com|access-date=2016-12-08}}</ref> Nibouar died in December 2017 at the age of 96.<ref>[https://www.legacy.com/obituaries/statesman/obituary.aspx?n=helen-lucile-breese-nibouar&pid=187686850&fhid=4296 Helen Lucile Breese Nibouar obituary]</ref>
